 LIVE  Updated  7m ago Simon Burnton Sat 14 Nov 2026 09.28 EST First published on Sat 14 Nov 2026 07.33 EST Share Key events 9m ago Half time: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City 
 10m ago GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City (Baltimore, 45+4 mins) 
 2h ago The teams! 
 2h ago Preamble 
 Ellie Carpenter surges forward on a Chelsea attack. Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Ellie Carpenter surges forward on a Chelsea attack. Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images Simon Burnton Sat 14 Nov 2026 09.28 EST First published on Sat 14 Nov 2026 07.33 EST Share Key events 9m ago Half time: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City 
 10m ago GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City (Baltimore, 45+4 mins) 
 2h ago The teams! 
 2h ago Preamble 
 7m ago 09.24 EST After just over half an hour the teams had had two shots each. In the final 15 minutes Chelsea outshot their opponents 4-0: they shut up shop in defence, worked a couple of half-chances, and finally took one.
 Here meanwhile are the lineups for the 3pm game:
 Tottenham Hotspur Women: Kop, Dijkstra, Koga, Amanda Nilden, Blakstad, Pelova, Spence, Hanson, Holdt, Gaupset, Tandberg. Subs: Panengstuen, Morris, Naz, Vinberg, Matilda Nilden, Gunning-Williams, Martinez, Wijk, Dezire-Pierre.
 Everton Women: Brosnan, Blundell, Layzell, Ishikawa, Kitagawa, Mace, Wheeler, Momiki, van Gool, Pacheco, Vignola. Subs: Foster, Hobson, Cain, Rantala, Mouchon, Finnigan, Galli, Silcock, Howard.
 Share 9m ago 09.22 EST Half time: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City
 45+6 mins: City dominated the opening exchanges but the game grew tighter and messier, until Sandy Baltimore blasted it open just before the break!
 Share 10m ago 09.21 EST GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City (Baltimore, 45+4 mins)
 Finally a shot on target, and there’s no stopping it! Baltimore gets the ball on the right of the area, Knaak doesn’t close her down, and she boshes a left-footer into the top, near cornner!
 View image in fullscreen Chelsea's Sandy Baltimore has a pop … Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen And ripples the back of the Manchester City net to open the scoring with the first shot of the match. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  09.28 EST 11m ago 09.19 EST 45+4 mins: Chelsea win the ball in the City defensive third but then completely waste it, and City get the chance to clear.
 Share 12m ago 09.18 EST 45+2 mins: A full two minutes passes between Shaw conceding a free-kick and Chelsea getting around to taking it. It’s lifted into the area, headed across goal, and collected by Yamashita.
 Share 15m ago 09.16 EST 45+1 mins: Into stoppage time, and there’s going to be about five minutes of it.
 Share 17m ago 09.14 EST 43 mins: It looks like Lauren Hemp is going to be able to continue, though she’s feeling the right side of her neck a little gingerly.
 Share 18m ago 09.12 EST 42 mins: The physios are back on, this time City’s, after Hemp landed awkwardly and stayed down.
 View image in fullscreen Lauren Hemp’s Manchester City teammates check on her. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA Share Updated at  09.24 EST 19m ago 09.11 EST 40 mins: Chance! It feels like it’s been a while since the last one, after the first quarter-hour or so was basically non-stop attacking. Anyway, Thompson crosses, and Beever-Jones meets it in the middle, but the ball’s a bit behind her, she has to improvise a goalwards volley and she can’t quite get it on target.
 Share 22m ago 09.08 EST 38 mins: Manchester United have, meanwhile, taken a 2-0 lead against Crystal Palace, thanks to Elisabeth Terland’s tidy finish.
 Share 25m ago 09.06 EST 36 mins: And Chelsea are forced into a second first-half substitution, with Aggie Beevor-Jones comes on for the injured Malard.
 Share 26m ago 09.05 EST 35 mins: Malard is now down and receiving treatment from Chelsea’s physios.
 Share 26m ago 09.04 EST 33 mins: Match stats so far: City have had 51% of possession, are 6-5 up on touches in the opposition box, the teams have had two shots each and none on target, and City have had 181 shots to Chelsea’s 175. In short, nothing between them.
 Share 28m ago 09.02 EST 31 mins: Chelsea escape, get down the other end and win a corner, which is floated into the area and looks to be curling in before Shaw gets the top of her head to it and diverts it wide!
 View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw clears her lines. Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.26 EST 30m ago 09.01 EST 29 mins: Most of the Chelsea team have spent most of the last few minutes within 30 yards of their own goal, but City haven’t been able to convert their possession into a chance.
 Share 33m ago 08.57 EST 26 mins: McCabe gives the ball away, and a couple of quick passes give Wamser a shooting chance from maybe 25 yards, but she can’t get it on target.
 Share 36m ago 08.54 EST 24 mins: So close! A fine pass finds Baltimore on the Chelsea left, and her low cross is just too far in front of Malard for her to turn it in!
 Share 38m ago 08.52 EST 21 mins: Chances for Chelsea! Thompson gets down the left but her Malard is being well marshalled by Knaak and her cross runs across the goalmouth to Carpenter, whose her cross is well cleared by Knaak.
 Share 42m ago 08.48 EST 18 mins: Chelsea have the ball for a while, which is something that didn’t really happen in an opening 10 minutes dominated by the visitors.
 Share 45m ago 08.46 EST 15 mins: A lovely pass releases Carpeneter down the Chelsea right, but once she gets to the edge of the area, and despite having three teammates offering options, she scuffs a feeble shot that rolls wide.
 Share 47m ago 08.44 EST 14 mins: A booking for Chelsea’s Lexi Potter, for fouling Coffey.
 Share 47m ago 08.43 EST 12 mins: Actually the ball came off Rose rather than Beney. Anyway, and more importantly, Chelsea have been forced to make a change in their defence with Buchanan being forced off, presumably through injury, and Buurman coming on.
 Share 50m ago 08.41 EST 10 mins: Another deflection nearly leads to a goal! Malard takes on Beney and runs into the area before sending in a cross the deflects off Beney and suddenly it’s heading in at the near post, but Yamashita reacts well, changes direction and makes the save.
 Share 51m ago 08.39 EST 9 mins: City are still pushing, and though McCabe has just denied Fujino another chance in doing so she so nearly deflected the ball into her own net! In the end it bounces just wide of the far post.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester City's Khadija Shaw shields the ball from Chelsea's Lucy Bronze. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  09.09 EST 52m ago 08.38 EST 8 mins: And another chance for Fujino! The ball cannons off a defender and into her path, allowing her to run clear and into the area, but she can’t find the net!
 Share 54m ago 08.37 EST 6 mins: Meanwhile the half-time whistle has sounded at the Progress with Unity Stadium, with Manchester United still 1-0 up against Crystal Palace.
 Share 55m ago 08.36 EST 5 mins: Then Chelsea go down the other end and Alyssa Thompson has an excellent chance to shoot from just outside the area, but it’s a poor effort and goes behind for a goal kick.
 Share 55m ago 08.35 EST 4 mins: Chance! Shaw, for the second time already, gets into space on the left of the area, and pulls back to Aoba Fujino, who shoots just wide!
 Share 1h ago 08.33 EST 2 mins: Buchanan lingers on the ball really unnecessarily inside her own penalty area, allowing Shaw to believe she can steal it, but then she toepokes it to a teammate just in time.
 Share 1h ago 08.31 EST 1 min: Peeeeeeep! Chelsea get the ball rolling!
 Share 1h ago 08.30 EST Almost gametime, as the referee checks her watch. And then her other watch.
 Share 1h ago 08.27 EST Liquidator rings out at Stamford Bridge as the two teams emerge!
 Share 1h ago 08.26 EST The two coaches have a little chat with the BBC. Here’s some of Sonia Bompastor:
 double quotation mark It’s the teams who are right now close to each other at the top of the table. We’re focused on winning the game. It’s still too early to focus on where we will be at the end of the season.
 And a bit of City’s Andree Jeglertz:
 double quotation mark Of course there’s some speed in their attacking phase. They also have a central midfielder who is dominating a lot of games. Both teams are playing a lot man-to-man in the defending phase, so you need to escape from that.
 Share 1h ago 08.18 EST After just over half an hour, Manchester United have had 79% of possession, 90% of the 10 shots, 100% of the two shots on target, and are generally in complete control.
 Share 1h ago 08.15 EST Before the United game Maya Le Tissier was given a framed shirt to mark her 150th appearance for the club. About 20 minutes later she had something else to celebrate.
 View image in fullscreen Maya Le Tissier of Manchester United poses for a photo with her 150 appearance award and Matt Johnson, United’s Director of Women’s Football Photograph: Charlotte Tattersall/WSL/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.31 EST 1h ago 08.04 EST Manchester United are dominating so far, and Maya Le Tissier has now put them 1-0 up with an excellent shot from 20 yards or so that dips into the corner of the net.
 View image in fullscreen Maya Le Tissier celebrates her fine strike. Photograph: Charlotte Tattersall/WSL/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.31 EST 2h ago 07.46 EST Essential pre-match reading: here’s Suzanne Wrack’s preview of Chelsea v Manchester City:
 There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique.
 But when Chelsea welcome the title holders and current league leaders to Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime the three points isn’t the most important takeaway. Instead, based on the state of play, it’s the momentum, confidence, belief and bragging rights that are critical.
 Much more here:
 Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think Read more Share 2h ago 07.45 EST Meanwhile, Manchester United’s home game against Crystal Palace is about to start. Victory would take United to within sniffing distance of London City Lionesses, currently third, while three points for Palace would propel them into the top half of the table.
 Share 2h ago 07.37 EST The teams!
 Team news has landed, and here are the lineups: 
 Chelsea Women: Hampton, Bronze, Buchanan, McCabe, Carpenter, Walsh, Potter, Thompson, Kaptein, Malard, Baltimore. Subs: Peng, Buurman, Nusken, Cuthbert, Bjorn, Las, Hamano, Brown, Beever-Jones.
 Man City Women: Yamashita, Beney, Rose, Knaak, Wamser, Coffey, Hasegawa, Fowler, Fujino, Hemp, Shaw. Subs: Cumings, Shimizu, Clinton, Mead, Miedema, Casparij, Blindkilde, Lohmann, Prior.
 Referee: Phoebe Cross.

 Allow and continue Share 2h ago 07.33 EST Preamble
 Hello world! So, it’s time. First against second, the club that won the league last season against the club that won the previous six in a row, and a game with the potential to define – and even decide – this season’s title race. Manchester City took over at the top of the table last week, when Lucy Bronze’s own-goal saw Chelsea drop two points – Everton managing to end a game in which they had 35% of possession, two touches in the opposition box (to Chelsea’s 55) and not even one single shot on target with a 1-1 draw – but there are only those two points between them, Chelsea have the better goal difference, and with the nearest challenger four points further back it seems likely, if not quite inevitable, that this season’s champions are playing in this game. There’s a long way to go, of course, but if City were to win, and stretch their lead to five points, it would take some overhauling.
 The really good news if this match does live up to expectations is that we won’t have to wait long for a second helping – there are only three rounds of WSL fixtures between this game and the return fixture at the Joie Stadium in January.
 Here’s the Press Association’s preview of this game, and the WSL weekend:
 Sonia Bompastor knows Chelsea will need to be “clinical” in their Women’s Super League clash with Manchester City.
 Saturday’s meeting between the top two takes place at Stamford Bridge and City enter the game as leaders having beaten West Ham 5-0 last weekend.
 Three points allowed City to move top after Chelsea were held to a 1-1 draw by Everton and the Blues endured further frustration this week with a goalless draw against Hacken in the Champions League.
 Chelsea dominated in Gothenburg but could not find the net and Bompastor admitted their last two games have been “frustrating”.
 She said: “It’s a good balance to have, to be able not to concede but also to be able to score.
 “I think the two last results have been frustrating for us so it’s good to see from the players’ reaction but also the staff reaction.
 “We have hunger going into the game tomorrow because I think at the end probably the Everton game was a game where we didn’t produce much on the pitch in terms of the attacking aspects.
 “Against Hacken, I think we were dominant in the game. So we need to keep working, I’m convinced tomorrow we’ll create opportunities and we will have to be clinical for sure. It’s an important game.”
 Only two points separate the teams and City boss Andree Jeglertz is looking forward to the occasion.
 He said: “I think these games are very special for everybody involved. We are really looking forward to an exciting day.”
 Jeglertz is hopeful that Niamh Charles, Beth Mead and Vivianne Miedema will be available.
 “All three of them actually were in the session (on Thursday) and I hope they will be available for Saturday,” Jeglertz added.
 “It looks good. We had a day off (on Wednesday) and (on Thursday) everybody is back, a good session, full of energy. I feel we are in a good place.”
 Saturday also sees Manchester United face Crystal Palace and Brighton host Liverpool, while fourth-placed Tottenham are aiming to build on back-to-back league wins when they come up against Everton.
 On Sunday, Aston Villa take on local rivals Birmingham and West Ham meet Charlton, who are yet to win a point this term.
 Third-placed London City Lionesses are also in action against Arsenal, with six points separating the two teams.
